#6291. 11 US Vacation Rentals Where the Hot Tub Comes With a View

Travelers love to debate window vs. aisle, or whether or not a group trip is a good idea, but I’ve never met anyone who didn’t love a hot tub. It’s the amenity that separates a good vacation home from a great one—the ultimate way to wake up your system in the morning or relax tired muscles in the evening, no matter the season. The rentals on this list, from cozy log cabins in Tennessee to glassy beach houses in coastal Oregon, all promise steamy hot tubs worth planning a trip around. Whether you want to experience the stillness of the New Mexican desert, breathe in the Blue Ridge mountain air, or look out for wildlife in Texas Hill Country, you can do it all from the comfort of your very own bubbling sanctuary. For a rejuvenating weekend away, where the agenda is resetting your nervous system or simply sharing a few laughs with friends, these hot tub–included rentals in the US are just the ticket.

We've selected these listings based on Superhost status, ratings, amenities, location, decor, editor stays, and previous guest reviews.

Number of guests: 10Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 3 bathsWhy we love it: In-unit washer/dryer, game room, outdoor space

Just a short drive away from some of Tennessee’s best theme parks (including Dollywood), this Smoky Mountain retreat is a home the entire family will love. The 2,100-square-foot cabin is divided into three levels, each with its own bedroom (all have king-size beds) and bathroom (one has a freestanding bathtub). Kids will love the game room in the loft, as well as a few hours spent at nearby Wild Bear Falls Indoor Water Park, Anakeesta, or Ripley's Aquarium of the Smokies. After all that fun, adults can end their days in the outdoor hot tub, perfectly positioned for watching the sun set over the mountain ridge.

Location: Gatlinburg, TennesseeThings to do nearby: Historic Ogle Log Cabin, Hillbilly Golf, Herbert Holt Park

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Pet-friendly, floor-to-ceiling windows, forest views

Ideal for a couples getaway in the woods, this glassy cabin, with its soaring, floor-to-ceiling windows, is sure to provide a nature-friendly reset. It’s located just a five-minute walk away from Hocking Hills State Park and has all the modern comforts you need: a newly renovated kitchen and dining area, a queen-size bed upstairs, and, of course, an outdoor patio with a firepit and hot tub for nights spent nestled in the trees. Many reviewers gush over how spotless the place is and how close it is to hiking trails. One thing to note: AWD/4WD vehicles are recommended due to the rugged landscape.

Location: Laurelville, OhioThings to do nearby: Hocking Hills State Park, Conkles Hollow State Nature Preserve, Cedar Falls

Number of guests: 10Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 3.5 bathsWhy we love it: Game room, home gym, lake views

This modern masterpiece of a home, perfect for large family gatherings, was voted a 2026 Vrbo Vacation Rental of the Year. And it’s pretty easy to understand why, between the gorgeous views of Squam Lake from nearly every corner; the private dock from which to swim, kayak, or paddleboard; and the hot tub that’s built into the property. There are dozens of hiking trails nearby, whether you want to go on an easy lakeside stroll or trek to Mount Morgan. Suitable for any season, the house invites you to either laze a sunny day away on the patio’s sun chairs or curl up by the fireplace on a cooler night.

Location: Center Harbor, New HampshireThings to do nearby: Lake Winnipesaukee, White Mountain National Forest, Loon Mountain Resort

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Cold plunge, meditation spaces, outdoor shower

For a Hudson Valley hideaway just minutes from Catskill State Park, this two-bedroom home is bound to bring you peace, with reading nooks, meditation spaces, and even a room for massages, which you can book alongside a sound bath. There’s plenty to do outside too, whether that looks like meandering along the nearby Mill Stream, stretching out on the “flying saucer” hammock, or engaging in a little hydrotherapy (there’s a cedar cold plunge and hot tub situated right next to each other). In the warmer months, roast some s’mores by the firepit, and in the winter months, read a book by the wood-burning stove.

Location: Woodstock, New YorkThings to do nearby: Catskill State Park, Hunter Mountain, Kaaterskill Falls

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Private balcony, barbecue, secluded location

Tucked away on six acres of Texas Hill Country, this cozy cabin is the ultimate Lone Star escape, with its vaulted ceilings, log walls, and cowhide rugs. Beyond the expansive living room and fully equipped kitchen, there’s a bedroom downstairs with a queen-size bed, plus another one upstairs with a king-size bed and private balcony. When night falls, take in the stars from the hot tub on the outdoor patio and keep an eye out for local wildlife, which can include deer, turkeys, birds, and the occasional fox. Enjoy the local shops and breweries of nearby Wimberley Square, or go swimming or hiking at Jacob’s Well and Blue Hole Regional Park.

Location: San Marcos, TexasThings to do nearby: Devil’s Backbone Tavern, Canyon Park, Jacob’s Well Natural Area

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Pet-friendly, in-unit washer/dryer, pool

Experience the beauty of the Yucca Valley desert from this spacious one-bedroom home. Just a 5-minute drive to Yucca Valley Community Park and a 15-minute drive to Joshua Tree National Park, it’s conveniently located for all kinds of desert excursions—there’s even a mountain of boulders right behind the home that guests can climb. Enjoy sunrise or sunset views from the outdoor stock tank pool or hot tub, and be sure to look out for animals. Previous guests have recorded a few sightings, from lizards and rabbits to coyotes and roadrunners.

Location: Yucca Valley, CaliforniaThings to do nearby: Yucca Valley Community Park, Hi-Desert Nature Museum, Desert Christ Park

Number of guests: 12Bed and bath: 5 bedrooms, 4 bathsWhy we love it: Ocean views, in-unit washer/dryer, proximity to beach

Located just north of Manzanita in Tillamook County, this massive, five-bedroom home offers spectacular views of Neahkahnie Beach. Suitable for a family reunion or bachelorette weekend, it can sleep up to 12 guests and has large spaces built for gathering, whether that’s the grand dining table near the kitchen or the patio outside that includes the gorgeous hot tub. There’s plenty to do nearby, from strolling down Manzanita’s Laneda Avenue in search of a quaint coffee shop to visiting the historic Nehalem Bay Winery for a tasting.

Location: Nehalem, OregonThings to do nearby: Sunset Beach, Oswald West State Park, Nehalem Bay State Park

Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Terrace, desert views, earthy interior design

At this El Prado property, you’ll have to make the tough call between hopping in the Japanese-style bathtub, the outdoor hot tub, or nearby Manby Hot Springs—but who says you can’t do all three? Located on 15 acres of land where juniper, piñon, and sage grow wild, the architectural home features cast-earth walls, a corrugated metal roof, radiant heat, and mahogany woodwork. Explore the many trails at Rio Grande Gorge National Monument, a minute’s walk away, then have a soak under the stars.

Location: El Prado, New MexicoThings to do nearby: Rio Grande del Norte National Monument, Manby Hot Springs, Taos Plaza

Number of guests: 12Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 3 bathsWhy we love it: Game room, pet-friendly, forest views

For a moment away in the Blue Ridge Mountains, look no further than Bear Pause Cabin, a three-bedroom retreat perfect for a multigenerational clan. Whether you want to play pool in the game room, take in views of the forest from the hot tub, or explore nearby Grandfather Mountain State Park, there’s no shortage of ways to spend your days. The fully equipped kitchen has everything you need to prepare meals at home, while the patio has a barbecue for outdoor entertaining. The wood-burning fireplace and blanket ladder in the living room make movie nights especially cozy.

Location: Seven Devils, North CarolinaThings to do nearby: Grandfather Vineyard & Winery, Grandfather Mountain State Park, Hawksnest Tubing Park

Number of guests: 16Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 4.5 bathsWhy we love it: Pet-friendly, in-unit washer/dryer, game room

This spacious four-bedroom home in Interlochen, Michigan, provides access to both Green Lake and the Betsie River. Inside, you’ll find vaulted ceilings, exposed beams, and large windows that give way to hues of blue and green. There are also a few dedicated spaces, like the “Mutt Room,” which features a custom dog shower, and the game room, with its ping-pong table. The house can fit up to 16 guests, thanks to the additional twin-size beds in a few of the bedrooms. Outside, you’ll find a hot tub, a firepit, a floating dock on the lake, a smaller riverside dock, and an anchored swim raft; guests can feel free to use the provided kayaks for a fun excursion.

Location: Interlochen, MichiganThings to do nearby: Green Lake, Interlochen Center for the Arts, Crystal Mountain

Number of guests: 10Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 3.5 bathsWhy we love it: Proximity to ski resorts, private deck, in-unit washer/dryer

If you’re planning a ski trip to Utah’s Deer Valley or Park City Mountain Resort, this bright and airy condo is an ideal place to retreat to after a day on the slopes. It boasts an entryway designed for gear drops, a spacious living area with a stone fireplace, and, the best part, an outdoor hot tub for the ultimate aprés-ski soak. While there are only three bedrooms, the home can actually sleep up to 10, thanks to the help of bunk beds and sleeper sofas. It’s time to take that ski trip out of the group chat.

Location: Park City, UtahThings to do nearby: Deer Valley Resort, Park City Mountain Resort, Homestead Crater

#6290. Frontier Shakes Up Leadership Team

Frontier is reshuffling its leadership team, hiring a new chief operating officer, and announcing the departures of two senior executives.

Michael Delehant will join the carrier as executive vice president and chief operating officer on Nov. 30. He will oversee all airline operations and report to CEO Jimmy Dempsey, Frontier said Monday.

Delehant most recently served as group managing director at Wizz Air, overseeing operational and commercial activities. He previously held senior positions at Vueling, including chief strategy and network officer, and worked in several leadership roles at Southwest.

Dempsey said Delehant’s experience would be “instrumental as we continue growing our airline and executing against our strategic priorities.”

The appointment comes as Trevor Stedke, senior vice president of operations, and Alex Clerc, senior vice president of customers, prepare to leave Frontier on Nov. 13. The airline did not give a reason for their departures in its announcement.

“I want to express my sincere gratitude to Trevor and Alex for their dedication and contributions to Frontier,” Dempsey said.

Frontier also promoted James Fenner to senior vice president and chief revenue officer. His responsibilities include pricing and revenue management, loyalty, and network planning.

Fenner has spent more than a decade at the airline, most recently serving as vice president of revenue and loyalty.

Bobby Schroeter will move into the role of senior vice president and chief marketing officer, overseeing the airline’s brand and customer experience. Both Fenner and Schroeter will report directly to Dempsey.

The changes follow Frontier’s third-quarter results, which showed a $104 million net loss, compared with a $77 million loss a year earlier. Excluding special items, the carrier reported a $40 million profit on record revenue of $1.36 billion.

It’s one thing to read about an exciting welcome offer and another to see what it can actually do in real life. So when the IHG One Rewards Premier Select Credit Card (see rates and fees) launched with a generous limited-time launch offer, I mapped it onto a weekend in New York City with my mom.

The card, now open to applicants, comes with a launch offer of 200,000 bonus points, earned after you spend $5,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening (apply by Nov. 18, 2026). Beyond the bonus, its benefits include automatic Platinum Elite status and up to $300 per year in food and beverage rewards at IHG Hotels.

But the real question for many IHG fans is how the welcome offer, benefits and earning rates stack up against an actual getaway.

My mom and I recently spent a mother-daughter weekend in New York City, staying two nights at the Kimpton Era Midtown New York and spending Saturday soaking up the city's art and culture. If you’re considering this card, here’s how our trip played out so you can see just how far all of these perks can go.

My mom had not visited New York in a long time, and I wanted to make sure we were right in the middle of the action while also being near great dining and activities. The Kimpton Era Midtown, which opened in early 2026 in a 33-story tower on West 48th Street, proved to be the perfect home base for us. The Theater District was within walking distance, and we were able to grab a quick subway ride uptown to the Met.

Our two-night weekend stay in New York would have cost 64,600 points per night, or 129,200 points total — versus $1,354 (including taxes and fees) if we'd paid cash.

That means the 200,000-point welcome offer would have covered our entire stay, and I would still have 70,800 points left over to put toward a future trip.

One thing to keep in mind: While we only had a weekend, you can plan a longer trip and take advantage of the fourth-night-free benefit (redeem points for three consecutive nights, get the fourth free) to make your points go even further.

Plus, each year on your cardholder anniversary, you get one free night certificate worth up to 60,000 points. If a night costs more than 60,000 points, IHG allows you to top off the additional points you need. For my stay at the Kimpton Era Midtown, I would have only needed an additional 4,600 points to cover one night, which would have been easy to earn as someone who frequently stays at IHG properties.

Nothing makes me feel more like a VIP at an IHG Hotel than my Platinum Elite Status. Cardholders get automatic IHG One Rewards Platinum Elite status for as long as they keep the card. That comes with perks such as room upgrades and early check-in when available.

Thanks to my loyalty, I applied for a Confirmable Suite Upgrade, one of the Milestone Rewards IHG One Rewards members can choose after reaching certain night thresholds in a calendar year. That means we checked in knowing a premium high-floor room with a view of the Empire State Building was waiting for us.

The surprises and delights didn’t end there, though. We were also given a welcome amenity as a thank-you for my status. I had the option to choose between 5,000 bonus points or a welcome beverage. I usually opt for points when I stay with IHG, but since we were celebrating our mother-daughter weekend, we decided to have some fun and treat ourselves to the welcome drinks.

One of the coolest perks on the IHG Premier Select Card is the $300 in annual Food and Beverage Rewards at IHG hotels, issued as a $75 voucher each calendar quarter. So before heading out for a full day of adventuring on Saturday, my mom and I enjoyed an awesome breakfast at Bar Rocco, and the $75 voucher would have covered our entire meal.

It’s important to note that any charges paid with a Food and Beverage Reward don't earn IHG points, but there are also a few other rules worth knowing to get the most out of this perk:

I booked our round-trip nonstop flights from Orlando International Airport (MCO) to LaGuardia Airport (LGA) directly with JetBlue for $422.85 per person. The IHG Premier Select Card offers a $200 statement credit each calendar year when you spend at least $250 on flights booked directly with an airline through Dec. 31, 2027.

Unlike some travel credits that tie you to a single carrier or a booking portal, this one works with any airline as long as you book directly, as I did. Plus, it’s a win-win because the remaining balance can be paid with the IHG Premier Select Card and earn 6 points per dollar since it counts as a travel purchase.

A weekend in New York City goes beyond the hotel stay. The IHG Premier Select Card helps you earn rewards on your flights, hotel stays and everything in between. This card gets you:

And these earning rates worked out well for our trip, right down to the experiences.

We spent Saturday morning at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, where admission for the two of us came to $60, and admired works by my personal favorite painter, Claude Monet, and explored the Temple of Dendur.

Our biggest splurge of the weekend, though, was on two tickets to see "Hamilton" at the Richard Rodgers Theatre, totaling $560. This was a real treat because original Broadway cast member Christopher Jackson (George Washington) temporarily rejoined for a limited engagement.

Since the IHG Premier Select Card earns 3 points per dollar on all other purchases, it will help you make the most of those experiences (and your souvenirs) too.

Our mother-daughter New York City weekend getaway is exactly the kind of trip that the new IHG One Rewards Premier Select Card was built for. And the welcome offer is the best way to make the most of it.

Right now, new cardholders can earn 200,000 bonus points after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening, but this limited-time launch offer is only available to those who apply by Nov. 18, 2026.

Beyond the welcome offer, the card's earning rates and benefits, such as the food and beverage reward and the $200 airline credit, keep the value coming long after you’ve used your points.

So if you stay at IHG hotels even a couple of times a year, then this card will likely be worth your while — and now is the perfect time to apply.

#6288. The 6 Best Airplane Bathrooms On Any Airline: The A380 Reigns Supreme

When most people think of airplane bathrooms, it’s probably not a nice image that comes to mind. Airlines have largely shrunk bathrooms on newer aircraft significantly, and at times they’re also not very well maintained.

That’s not true across the board, though. In premium cabins, we’ve seen airlines introduce some pretty amazing amenities in recent years, and that even includes awesome bathrooms.

In this post, I’d like to share what I consider to be the airlines with the best first class bathrooms (somewhat overlapping with my list of the world’s best first class airlines).

Unsurprisingly, the Airbus A380 takes center stage on this flight, as it’s an aircraft that has ushered in the most bathroom innovation. That’s because the front of the upper deck has a bit of extra space that can’t be utilized for seats, making room for some cool amenities.

With that in mind, below are my six favorite airplane bathrooms, roughly ranked…

Emirates A380 first class is one of my all-around favorite first class products, and a large part of that is the amazing A380 first class shower suites.

Emirates’ A380s have two first class shower suites at the front of the upper deck, equipped with heated floors, enough amenities to start a toiletry resale business, and most importantly, a shower.

As a first class passenger, you can schedule a shower at the beginning of your flight, and while there’s no time limit to how long you can use the shower spa, you’re limited to five minutes of water. Fortunately you can turn the water on and off without the clock “running,” so that’s more than enough water for a nice shower.

Of all the excitement I’ve experienced in the air, I don’t think anything compares to the first time I took a shower on Emirates. The airline even has shower spa attendants, who make sure the shower spas are well maintained throughout the flight.

Etihad A380 first class consists of nine “First Class Apartments,” and these passengers have access to the shower suite at the front of the cabin. Much like on Emirates, each passenger gets five minutes of water, and the shower suite is refreshed between each use.

While this is a great and refreshing feature, the shower suite definitely isn’t as spacious as on Emirates. So if you’re used to showering on Emirates, you might find that it’s a bit tight, but otherwise you’ll no doubt be delighted. Also keep in mind that there’s still The Residence on Etihad, which is a three room suite that can be reserved as an upgrade over the standard first class. This comes with a private bathroom, including shower.

Singapore Airlines A380 Suites is an incredible first class product, with only six seats in the cabin. While you won’t find a shower on Singapore Airlines’ A380s, you will find some of the most spacious bathrooms in the sky. One of the lavatories has a huge vanity, and is probably the size of 10 typical Boeing 737 MAX bathrooms. Airplane bathrooms don’t get much more luxurious than this!

Qatar Airways A380 first class has two very nice lavatories at the front of the upper deck. While there aren’t any special amenities, you’ll find that they’re incredibly spacious, and nicely decorated.

Lufthansa A380 first class features two huge lavatories at the front of the upper deck, each equipped with a bench, and most excitingly, a urinal! Lufthansa is the only airline to offer urinals on planes, so that’s pretty special… or something.

While we’re speaking of Lufthansa, I have a soft spot for Lufthansa 747-8 first class, probably at least partly because the Boeing 747-8 is my favorite plane as an avgeek. While not quite as over the top as some of the other options, Lufthansa’s 747-8 lavatories are spacious, have a bench you can extend out over the toilet, and most importantly, have a window. It’s so nice to be able to look out the window while in the lavatory.

Lastly on the topic of Lufthansa and lavatories, I do have to bring up how cool the economy lavatories on the carrier’s A340-600s were (these planes were just recently retired). They were located on the “lower deck” (in a cargo compartment), so they were probably the most unusual lavatories you could’ve recently found in commercial service. By comparison, the Lufthansa A340 first class lavatories weren’t much to get excited about at all.

All Nippon Airways A380 first class has two large, identical lavatories at the front of the upper deck. They’re huge, but there are also a couple of thoughtful design touches that I appreciate about them.

For one, ANA has a bidet function for its toilets, which is always a nice feature to have. I also appreciate how there’s a “plank” of sorts that you can extend on the ground, for situations where you want to change into pajamas without touching the regular floor of the bathroom.

On top of that, ANA does an amazing job with keeping its lavatories clean between each use, down to folding the toilet paper into perfect triangles.

Now, in fairness, there are a decent number of products with a bidet function in service, from Japan Airlines A350 first class, to Gulf Air 787 business class, to Oman Air 787 business class.

There are some pretty incredible airplane bathrooms out there. While nothing can compete with Emirates’ amazing shower suites, there are plenty of other impressive airplane bathrooms out there as well, with everything from vanities, to bidets, to urinals. As A380s increasingly get retired, unfortunately going to the bathroom on a plane is getting less pleasant!

What’s your favorite bathroom on a commercial aircraft?

#6287. Air India CEO Wants ‘More Widebody Aircraft’

Air India is looking to buy more widebody jets as it expands overseas and works to return to profitability.

“We want more widebody aircraft,” CEO Tewolde Gebremariam said Tuesday at the Aviation India and South Asia summit in New Delhi, according to Reuters. The carrier has held talks with both Airbus and Boeing. Gebremariam did not say how many aircraft Air India might buy.

The airline’s most recent Boeing order, announced in January, was for 30 narrowbodies: 20 737 MAX 8s and 10 MAX 10s.

The carrier is also updating the widebodies it already flies. In April, Air India took delivery of the first of 26 older Boeing 787-8s slated for cabin retrofits. The aircraft went from two cabins to three with the addition of premium economy.

Gebremariam, who previously led Ethiopian Airlines, described high operating costs as a “major concern” but said he expects Air India to return to profitability “very soon.”

Air India Group lost S$3.56 billion in the fiscal year ended March 31, according to financial disclosures from Singapore Airlines, which owns a 25% stake in the group. The loss came as the carrier dealt with disruption from the war in Iran and Pakistan’s closure of its airspace to Indian airlines.

#6286. Arc'teryx Promo Codes & Deals November 2026

Whether you’re a seasoned mountaineer, a proponent of gorpcore, or a mix of both, you’re probably familiar with the Vancouver-based outdoors brand Arc’teryx (Did you know it was named after the Archaeopteryx lithographica, the first reptile to develop feathers for flight?). Famous for its waterproof Gore-Tex shell jackets, down parkas, and—if you’re a Brooklyn hipster—the iconic Bird Head Toque hat, the brand is committed to developing the very best in activewear technology, often testing its gear on the Coast Mountains of British Columbia for durability, comfort, and function.

Founded in 1989 by Dave Lane as “Rock Solid,” the brand started out as a collection of climbing harnesses. After enlisting Jeremy Guard, the company was rebranded as “Arc’Teryx” in 1991, with a new logo: a stylized skeleton of the Archaeopteryx lithographica. In 1998, the brand secured a license for Gore-Tex, launching the iconic Alpha SV jacket. In the last few years, Arc’teryx has made its way into high fashion, capturing the attention of street-style icons behind the gorpcore trend and collaborating with designers like Jil Sander. While Arc’teryx gear does cost a pretty penny, there are all kinds of deals to look out for to help you save big on your next purchase. (While these discounts come directly from the brand, keep in mind outdoor outfitter REI is currently offering significant discounts on various Arc'teryx apparel). Below, find the best Arc’teryx discounts, promo codes, and offers.

Before you commit to buying something full-price, have a look at the Arc’teryx Outlet, where you can score up to 50% off a selection of men's and women’s shell jackets, base layers, and footwear—including products from Veilance, the brand’s more urban-friendly line. Men, for instance, can currently save 30% on the Solano jacket, as well as 65% on the Kragg shoe. For the steepest discounts, keep an eye out for discontinued colors and previous iterations of core products. Keep in mind, though, that all items purchased at the Arc’teryx Outlet are final sale.

Part of Arc’teryx’s commitment to sustainability is ensuring products last for lifetimes. When you trade in gently used Arc’teryx gear, you’ll receive a gift card worth 30% of the original retail value. Trade-ins are processed through the Rebird Resale program—simply complete the trade-in form online to get a shipping label, then package the gear and mail it in, or drop it off in store to save on shipping fees. Only eligible items will qualify for the trade-in, so those that pose hygiene issues, like cotton T-shirts or headwear, are less likely to be accepted. A good rule of thumb is that if you wouldn’t gift it to a friend, it likely won’t be eligible.

Through Arc’teryx’s Pro Program, qualified outdoor experts and community partners—including mountain guides, park rangers, firefighters, ski instructors, and more—can take advantage of special discounted pricing. To apply, fill out an application and verify your professional credentials on the Arc’teryx site.

Arc’teryx offers free shipping on all orders placed within the US—no minimum purchase required. This includes items from the Arc’teryx Outlet, and also extends to free returns within a 30-day window for most purchases. Whether you’re grabbing a pair of merino wool hiking socks or a comfortable jacket for day hikes, the price on the tag (plus tax) is all you’ll be paying.

To get the best possible deal, combine savings strategies. Use trade-in credits from the Rebird program on items already marked down in the Outlet, and check the Outlet regularly, since new styles rotate in often. Sign up for the brand newsletter to receive alerts on upcoming Arc'teryx savings opportunities.

#6285. Qatar Launches Two South American Destinations

Qatar Airways added two South American destinations on Wednesday, becoming the first Gulf carrier to serve Venezuela.

The new service flies from Doha to Bogotá, Colombia, then continues to Caracas, Venezuela, before returning nonstop to Doha. Qatar Airways will operate the route on Wednesdays and Sundays using a Boeing 777-200LR.

Flights are scheduled to leave Doha at 7:35 a.m. and reach Bogotá at 4:25 p.m. After a 90-minute stop, the aircraft continues to Caracas, arriving at 9 p.m. The return flight leaves Caracas at 11:30 p.m. and reaches Doha at 8:35 p.m. the following day. All times are local.

The airline originally planned to start flying the route in July but postponed the launch following an earthquake in Venezuela, according to Aviation Week.

Qatar Airways is also expanding its codeshare with LATAM to include domestic flights from Bogotá. The agreement will put Qatar’s code on LATAM flights to destinations including Medellín, Cartagena and Cali.

The additions bring Qatar Airways’ network in the Americas to 17 destinations. The carrier began serving South America in 2010 with flights to São Paulo.

#6284. 6 Airlines Offering Premium Economy On Flights Shorter Than 6 Hours

What do passengers expect from a modern airline cabin? Long-haul widebodies typically feature dedicated multi-cabin layouts, while short-haul regional hops stick to strict two-class narrowbodies. However, evolving passenger expectations and fleet-utilization strategies have disrupted that boundary. Across high-density regional and transcontinental corridors, a growing number of major carriers are selling international-grade premium economy seats on sectors lasting under six hours.

The trend provides an intriguing value proposition for travelers heading on three to five-hour flights. Rather than paying a substantial markup for short-haul business class or sacrificing personal space in a high-density economy cabin, flyers can find wider seats, additional legroom, and enhanced dining at a fraction of the cost. Still, as airlines deploy long-haul widebodies and long-range narrowbodies on regional trunk routes, availability often hinges on specific aircraft swaps and seasonal scheduling.

As detailed in a cabin review by Point Hacks, Cathay Pacific’s A350 premium economy layout features a 2-4-2 arrangement providing 40 inches (102 cm) of seat pitch and 19 inches (48 cm) of seat width. The airline also schedules these widebodies on four to five-hour overnight red-eye flights to Japan, Singapore, and Indonesia. Furthermore, as reported by The Alviator, Cathay Pacific has integrated its newly redesigned Boeing 777-300ER premium economy cabins into short-haul regional rotations connecting Hong Kong to Tokyo Haneda Airport (HND), New Chitose Airport (CTS), and Beijing Capital Airport (PEK).

However, when booking regional premium economy on Cathay Pacific, it is important to pay close attention to daily equipment schedules. The carrier regularly rotates regionally configured Airbus A330-300s and regional A350s onto these same intra-Asia routes, which lack a premium economy section entirely.

Air New Zealand frequently deploys its long-haul Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners across the trans-Tasman sea to connect Auckland Airport (AKL) with key Australian hubs like Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (SYD) and Melbourne Airport (MEL). Ranging from three to four hours, these short-haul international hops feature a dedicated 41 inches (104 cm) seat pitch in premium economy, delivering significantly more legroom than standard domestic offerings.

Analysis published by Simple Flying notes that Air New Zealand’s trans-Tasman premium economy is often the smartest buy for passengers, evaluating price versus comfort. Because the short flight duration makes a full lie-flat bed in Business Premier less essential, the generous recline, dedicated footrests, and premium dining in premium economy deliver most long-haul benefits at a much lower price.

As a result, Air New Zealand can maximize aircraft utilization between major long-haul rotations to North America and Asia. Offering international-grade seating on short daytime hops, the carrier fills mid-cabin capacity with high-yielding business and leisure travelers. What is important to keep in mind is that this regional widebody strategy is not unique to Oceania and is equally prominent across key trunk corridors in Southeast Asia.

More space, better meals, and none of the business class price tag — but only if you know which airline to book.

Singapore Airlines regularly deploys long-haul widebodies across its regional network, connecting its Changi hub with high-density commercial markets across Asia. On the 1,588-mile (2,555 km) trunk route between Singapore and Hong Kong, a flight lasting roughly four hours, the carrier regularly sends its long-haul-configured A350-900 and 777-300ER aircraft. These airframes feature dedicated premium economy cabins offering 38 inches (97 cm) of seat pitch and up to 19.5 inches (50 cm) of seat width, providing a spacious middle-tier option for regional business travelers.

As reported by Simple Flying, Singapore Airlines periodically increases capacity on this four-hour regional corridor by deploying its flagship Airbus A380 during peak travel seasons. Positioned as the shortest A380 route in the carrier's global network, these double-decker superjumbos feature a dedicated main-deck premium economy cabin outfitted in a 2-4-2 layout. Passengers on these short-haul rotations are given full long-haul hardware amenities, including 13.3-inch (34 cm) HD seatback monitors, calf rests, and leather seating finishes.

However, booking a premium economy seat on Singapore Airlines' short-haul routes also comes with frequent aircraft changes. The airline also operates medium-haul A350-900 variants across its regional network, which are configured in a two-class setup that lacks premium economy entirely. Generally, Asian carriers use widebodies to solve regional slot constraints, whereas major US legacy airlines form their fleet on a mix of repositioning widebodies and next-generation narrowbodies to bring premium economy to domestic transcontinental markets.

In North America, Delta Air Lines has introduced its international-grade Delta Premium Select cabin onto select domestic transcontinental corridors. Delta does not limit the product strictly to long-haul transoceanic flights and offers Premium Select on key hub-to-hub transcontinental rotations, such as New York John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) and San Francisco International Airport (SFO). On these 2,475-mile (3,983 km) transcontinental links, flight times vary directionally as eastbound flights from the West Coast regularly clock in under five hours and 30 minutes, while westbound sectors into winter headwinds can occasionally approach the six-hour mark.

According to a review published by Going, Delta Premium Select on domestic transcontinental routes provides a distinct upgrade over Delta Comfort+. With customized recline seats offering up to 38 in (97 cm) of pitch and 19 in (48 cm) of width, the cabin includes dedicated footrests, improved dining options, and priority boarding. Delta operates internationally configured widebodies, such as the Boeing 767-400ER and Airbus A330-900, on these premier domestic transcontinental routes, so travelers actually can get access to long-haul hardware on sub-six-hour sectors.

Delta Premium Select is sold on only select daily JFK–LAX rotations rather than every frequency, as noted by The Points Guy. The carrier mixes widebody operations with domestic narrowbodies that offer standard first class and Comfort+ seating instead. As North American carriers expand transcontinental premium offerings, the introduction of long-range narrowbodies like the Airbus A321XLR is set to make short-haul premium economy even more widespread.

Singapore Airlines removed economy from its longest flights but kept premium economy. The routes where premium seats matter may surprise you.

United Airlines has expanded its dedicated international Premium Plus cabin onto high-density domestic transcontinental routes connecting its primary hub network. On key sub-six-hour transcontinental corridors, such as Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) to San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Chicago O'Hare International Airport(ORD) to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), United regularly schedules internationally configured widebodies, including 777-200ERs and 787-10s. Deploying these widebody aircraft on domestic hub-to-hub legs brings long-haul hardware directly to transcontinental travelers.

As detailed in routing and pricing analysis from Autopilot, United’s Premium Plus cabin features a 2-4-2 layout on widebodies, offering 38 in (97 cm) of seat pitch and 19 in (48 cm) of seat width. Passengers receive plush leather recline seats, footrests, individual power outlets, and upgraded inflight entertainment screens. On competitive transcontinental routes, United's Premium Plus tickets sit at a median price markup of $733 over standard economy, capturing high-yield corporate travelers whose companies restrict lie-flat business class bookings on sub-six-hour sectors.

United is further solidifying this domestic middle tier with the delivery of its A321XLR fleet. Configured with 12 dedicated Premium Plus seats in a 2-2 layout on narrowbody frames, the A321XLR allows United to offer consistent long-haul Premium Plus hardware on sub-six-hour transcontinental sectors without relying solely on widebody repositioning flights.

American Airlines is at the forefront of domestic transcontinental travel, deploying its purpose-built A321XLR fleet across premium sub-six-hour corridors. As detailed in operational analysis by Cirium, American has configured its A321XLR with a dedicated 12-seat premium economy cabin positioned between Flagship Suites and Main Cabin Extra. Scheduled on prime transcontinental routes such as New York (JFK) to San Francisco (SFO) and Boston (BOS) to Los Angeles (LAX), these five to six-hour sectors will see a move toward long-haul cabin hardware on single-aisle aircraft.

The 12-seat premium economy cabin on American’s A321XLR features a spacious 2-2 layout outfitted with Recaro seating platforms. Passengers enjoy 37 in (94 cm) of seat pitch, deep recline mechanisms, integrated leg and footrests, and 13.3-inch 4K touchscreen entertainment displays. Delivering true long-haul seating comfort, premium dining, and priority airport handling on sub-six-hour transcontinental flights, American provides a compelling middle-tier alternative for travelers seeking comfort without paying business class rates.

The introduction of dedicated premium economy cabins on short-haul and transcontinental sectors is equally being seen across the global aviation industry. Whether it be traveling on intra-Asia widebody routes or North American narrowbody transcontinental corridors, flyers no longer have to cross oceans to experience long-haul seating comfort. More and more airlines are now looking to expand custom-configured fleets like the A321XLR, so sub-six-hour premium economy will increasingly become the standard benchmark for regional premium flying.

#6283. Flagship Dining: American Expands A La Carte Lounge Dining To Business Class

Several weeks back, American announced plans to completely change the concept for its Flagship First Dining facilities, as the airline eliminates international first class. With this, we’re seeing Flagship First Dining simply rebranded as Flagship Dining, with business class passengers also getting access.

While these changes went “live” as of September 15, 2026, there’s now an additional update, as a third Flagship Dining facility has just opened, so you can now enjoy this experience in Dallas (DFW), Los Angeles (LAX), and Miami (MIA). Let’s cover all the details.

For years, American had Flagship First Dining, which are facilities inside select Flagship Lounges. The idea was that this offers an a la carte dining experience for those traveling in international or premium transcontinental first class.

American is currently in the process of eliminating “premium” first class — Boeing 777-300ERs are being reconfigured without first class, while Airbus A321XLRs (without first class) are replacing A321Ts. First class is no longer being sold on the wide bodies as of November 19, 2026, or on the narrow bodies as of March 28, 2027. So there has been a big question as to what American would do with these facilities in the future. Would they just close, or what? Well, it’s much better than that.

As of September 15, 2026, Flagship First Dining has simply become Flagship Dining, and the idea is that this is now open to all Flagship Business passengers traveling on qualifying long haul international, transcontinental, and Hawaii flights.

In other words, if you have access to a Flagship Lounge on account of your American business class ticket, you’re also eligible for Flagship Dining, on a space available basis. However, if you have Flagship Lounge access on account of elite status, or through traveling in a premium cabin on a partner airline, you wouldn’t have access to this facility.

American notes how guests interested in dining should check in with the host team inside the Flagship Lounge upon arrival. If a table is immediately available, guests will be seated at that time. If all tables are occupied, guests may be added to an electronic waitlist and will be notified when their table is ready. Tables will be offered on a first come, first served basis, and as I understand it, there’s no priority for first class passengers, Concierge Key members, etc.

I would expect that demand will greatly exceed supply, especially during peak hours. However, the same is true for the a la carte dining in United Polaris Lounges and (to a lesser extent) at some Delta One Lounges. This is really a great way for American to become more competitive with Delta and United. I’m really, really impressed, and this seems like a sincere effort to improve the premium experience.

Launching alongside the expanded dining facility access is an all-new four-course Flagship Dining menu. The airline promotes that “the seasonal offerings blend regional flavors, thoughtfully sourced ingredients and refined culinary techniques to create an elevated dining experience inspired by some of the world’s most celebrated restaurants.”

American is sharing some of the dishes that will be on offer, including a Texas pear and burrata salad…

In addition to that, American is introducing a wine and chocolate pairing, featuring KHK Wines and K+M Extravirgin Chocolate. Chef Thomas Keller, who co-founded K+M Extravirgin Chocolate with Italian olive oil producer Armando Manni, curated the pairing.

American has launched Flagship Dining, essentially a rebranding and repurposing of the Flagship First Dining facilities. This is being done because American is eliminating “premium” first class in the coming months.

This means American is now offering proper a la carte dining in its business class lounges, increasingly matching the competition. What an awesome change from American! You can find these facilities in Dallas, Los Angeles, and Miami.

What do you make of the evolved Flagship Dining concept? If you visit a Flagship Dining facility, please report back with your experience (food quality, wait times, etc.)!

#6281. Qantas Reaches Deal to Sell 44 Boeing 737s

Qantas has agreed to sell 44 Boeing 737-800s to British aviation aftermarket specialist AerFin as the Australian carrier prepares to retire most of its 737 fleet.

The deal includes the aircraft’s 88 CFM56-7B engines. AerFin said Wednesday it expects to receive the first jet before the end of 2026, with the rest transferring over the next seven years as Qantas retires them.

Qantas Domestic CEO Markus Svensson said the agreement gives the airline “flexibility to adjust the timing as new aircraft arrive,” in a news release.

Qantas operates nearly 80 Boeing 737-800s, according to data from planespotters.net. The carrier ordered 28 Airbus A321XLRs in 2022 to begin replacing the Boeing jets and later ordered another 20. Seven A321XLRs have joined the fleet, with 41 still on order.

AerFin, which supplies parts and engines to airlines and maintenance providers, said the acquisition is the largest in its history. The company said the deal would help it supply aircraft and engine parts to customers worldwide.

#6279. Allegiant Says MAX 7 Seat Cost ‘Loses Pace’

Allegiant prefers the economics of the Boeing 737 MAX 8 over the smaller MAX 7 as its plans for premium seating change how it evaluates the two aircraft.

The MAX 7 originally accounted for the majority of Allegiant’s Boeing commitment. In January 2022, the airline announced an order for 50 aircraft, split between 30 MAX 7s and 20 high-density MAX 8-200s, with options for another 50 jets.

The agreement, signed in December 2021, was Allegiant’s first direct Boeing order and marked a shift for a carrier that had largely built its business around buying used aircraft. At the time of the announcement, Allegiant operated 108 Airbus A319s and A320s.

Boeing said the new jets would reduce fuel consumption by about 20% compared with the older Airbus aircraft.

Speaking during the carrier’s third-quarter earnings call Wednesday, President and Chief Financial Officer Robert Neal said the MAX 7 initially offered an attractive balance between the cost of operating each flight and the cost per seat.

“When we did the order, we really liked the MAX 7 because we were looking at both the MAX 8 and MAX 7 at very high density,” Neal said. “And so you’ve got a really nice trip cost seat cost mix with the MAX 7.”

That calculation has changed as Allegiant expands its extra-legroom Allegiant Extra product and prepares to introduce Allegiant First.

“But over time, as you’ve seen us roll out incremental premium offerings at the moment through Allegiant Extra and eventually with Allegiant First, the seat cost just sort of loses pace with the MAX 8,” Neal said. “And so we prefer the cost economics of the MAX 8 at this point.”

Allegiant began shifting its order toward the larger variant in September 2023. An amended agreement retained the 50 firm aircraft but increased the number of MAX 8-200s, reduced the number of MAX 7s and expanded the option pool to 80 aircraft.

The MAX 7 faced years of certification delays, including work to redesign its engine anti-ice system. The FAA approved the variant on Aug. 3, after requiring changes to that system, flight-control software, and cockpit alerts.

The ultra-low-cost carrier added to its MAX 8 commitments last month, exercising six options for delivery in 2028. That brought its firm Boeing order to 56 aircraft, including 22 delivered through Oct. 23, with 74 options remaining.

#6278. Finland Is Throwing an Epic Dinner Party for 16 Singles—Here's How to Get Invited

The Nordic countries are well known for their rather gimmicky yet innovative travel campaigns luring travelers to the icy north. From doctors prescribing travel to Sweden as a medical treatment to Oslo's viral mock-documentary narrated by a jaded local called Halfdan. Preceding these by a decade, Danish tour operator Spies Travels famously promoted its ”Do It for Denmark!” campaign focused on Denmark’s low birth rates, offering “ovulation discounts” to couples who proved they conceived on their romantic trip.

Now, Finland has announced it's flying out sixteen international singles this February for a "blind group date with likeminded travelers and local Finnish singles.”

The country is touting the so-called Love At First Bite campaign as an epic blind dinner date, designed to help participants “discover Finnish food, meet new people, and perhaps even find love.” The singles will be divided and hosted in two group dates in capital city Helsinki and Tampere located in Europe’s largest lake district, Finland’s Lakeland region.

Joining the singles over candlelit tasting menus crafted by local celebrity chefs will be local single Finns. Get ready for lots of prolonged eye contact—the Nordic way of flirting—under low light as you bond over the likes of wild trout, reindeer, chanterelle mushrooms, and sea buckthorn. For those heading to Tampere, the destination is monikered the “world’s sauna capital,” so chances of sweating with your fellow single strangers is probably on the menu too.

I’ll admit, when the campaign was launched worldwide, my Finnish friends and I wrinkled our noses in confusion. Romantic and sexy aren’t the first words that come to mind when you think of Finland. And it's not the Nordic country you'd first go to for love if we're talking stereotypes. The Danes have their extroverted charm, the Swedes their chic worldliness, and the Norwegians typically have more money to spend on you. Popular Nordic comedians Helgi and Erlend riff on these regional stereotypes, depicting their Finnish character as stoic, quiet and mentally tough. The very Finnish ethos of “sisu” means grit and the tenacity to push through tough times. But maybe those are qualities you'd want in a lifelong partner as you navigate challenges together.

So the campaign got me thinking a little deeper. Named the happiest country in the world for the ninth consecutive year in a row, Finns are satisfied with their lifestyles firmly rooted in the outdoors, nature, and a slower pace of life. In this contentment is where you’ll find Finland’s hidden sexier side.

In a country of roughly five million, there are two million saunas. And few places are more intimate than sweating together naked in a sauna, dipping in chilly lakes during winter, then warming back up indoors in many more ways. There’s also something rather romantic about grilling wild-caught salmon for two over an open flame in the backcountry.

This isn’t the first time the country has dabbled in an unconventional approach to dating. The viral “Sinkkukori” phenomenon introduced pink shopping baskets as a way for singles to covertly signal their availability. Now Finland is taking a more overt approach to romance. As the well-known nineteenth-century English idiom reminds us, the quickest way to the heart is through the stomach, and Finland certainly wants to put this to the test.

To shoot your shot at finding love in Finland, apply by November 10, 2026 at 11:59 AM Finnish time. All you have to do is make a video answering the question: what would you serve on a dinner date, and why? Just like a proper prospect, Finland would like to know your preferences in advance so it can woo you in the most epic and intentional way. If that isn’t romantic, I don’t know what is.

#6277. Qantas Is Training 360+ Pilots & 1,200 Cabin Crew For Just 12 Airbus A350-1000ULRs

Brandon's passion for aviation started at a young age. He became involved in the flight simulator and VATSIM communities, which sparked his interest in aviation and eventually led him to earn his private pilot license. Outside of work, he continues to build flight hours, explore new airports, and stay involved in the aviation community.

Qantas will train more than 360 pilots and 1,200 cabin crew to operate 12 aircraft. The figure comes from the airline's own announcement, which states both groups will be trained by the time the twelfth Airbus A350-1000ULR arrives. That works out to 30 pilots and 100 cabin crew per airframe, roughly double what a conventional long-haul aircraft requires, on a fleet carrying 238 passengers per flight.

The length of the flights explains the ratio. Each aircraft carries an additional 5,283-gallon (20,000-liter) rear center fuel tank, enabling more than 9,942 miles (16,000 km) and up to 22 hours nonstop; a sector that long requires more pilots on board and longer rest periods afterward than any conventional rotation. Training is already underway on Australia's first A350 simulator in Sydney and with British Airways in the UK, drawn initially from Qantas A330 pilots, 40 of whom are converting to the A350 while continuing to fly their existing aircraft. The first A350-1000ULR arrives in April 2027, with Sydney to London launching that October and Sydney to New York from mid-2028.

Qantas will train more than 360 pilots and 1,200 cabin crew to operate 12 aircraft. The figure comes from the airline's announcement, which says both groups will be trained by the time the twelfth A350-1000ULR arrives. Divided across the fleet, that is 30 pilots and 100 cabin crew for every airframe, on aircraft configured with 238 seats each.

The ratio is unusual enough that it drew attention when Qantas published it. Across the full Project Sunrise fleet, the airline is committing to a flight and cabin crew workforce of more than 1,560 people for twelve aircraft, a number driven by the operating profile rather than the fleet size.

The scale also reflects what Qantas is building toward, not what it needs on day one. Project Sunrise is the airline's first attempt at operating ultra-long-range flights as a core part of the network rather than a record-setting exception, and the 1,560 figure covers the full twelve-aircraft fleet across London, New York and whatever routes follow. Qantas has said the program forms part of a broader fleet renewal that shifts the carrier from a predominantly Boeing-operated long-haul fleet to a largely Airbus-based structure, which means the training effort extends beyond Project Sunrise itself and into how the airline's entire long-haul operation will be crewed over the next decade.

The A350-1000ULR has an additional 20,000-liter rear center fuel tank that lets it fly more than 16,000 km and up to 22 hours nonstop. Qantas describes the aircraft as purpose-built for that mission, and the crew numbers follow from it rather than from the size of the fleet.

Qantas has framed the operation around the science of ultra-long-haul travel. Group CEO Vanessa Hudson described the aircraft as representing a fundamentally different way to fly, citing the lighting, the meals and a world-first Wellbeing Zone designed to help passengers manage flights of this length. The cabin holds 238 seats across four classes, comprising 6 first, 52 business, 40 premium economy and 140 economy.

Regulatory arrangements for flights of this duration are also distinct from standard long-haul operations. Qantas has worked with the Civil Aviation Safety Authority on fatigue management for ultra-long-range flying, an area where normal duty limits do not straightforwardly apply to sectors exceeding 20 hours. The specifics of how crew complements and duty periods are set for Project Sunrise have not been published in detail, but the scale of the workforce Qantas has committed to training is the clearest public indication of what operating a 22-hour sector requires compared with a conventional long-haul rotation. The airline has also not disclosed how crews will be based or how rostering will distribute flying across the 360 pilots, both of which shape how many people a daily London rotation actually consumes. What is clear from the published figure is that Qantas expects to need substantially more crew per aircraft than its existing long-haul fleet requires, and that the gap grows with every additional ultra-long-haul route the program adds.

Anticipation is growing for Project Sunrise, which is set to launch in 2027.

Qantas pilots began training on Australia's first A350 simulator, installed in Sydney, ahead of the aircraft's arrival. The airline has also sent pilots to train with British Airways in the United Kingdom, which operates the A350-1000 and can provide experience that does not yet exist in Australia. Running both tracks lets Qantas build A350 competency before it has an aircraft of its own.

The initial cohort comes from inside the existing fleet. Qantas's current A330 pilots make up the first intake for Project Sunrise, with 40 already in the process of training for the A350 alongside their existing A330 flying.

Timing adds pressure to it all. With first delivery in April 2027 and Sydney to London launching that October, Qantas has roughly six months between receiving its first aircraft and operating a revenue service on the longest route in its network. Reporting on the program suggests the first A350-1000ULR will likely fly to New Zealand for training and crew familiarization before entering scheduled ultra-long-haul service, which gives crews time on the actual aircraft on short sectors before they take it to London. Everything before that point happens in a simulator in Sydney or on another airline's aircraft in the United Kingdom.

Project Sunrise takes its name from the Double Sunrise endurance flights Qantas operated during the Second World War, a reference the airline has made explicitly in describing the program. The modern version aims to connect Australia's east coast nonstop to London and New York, routes no airline has operated without a stop.

The timeline has been long and repeatedly extended. Qantas announced in December 2019 that its preferred aircraft for the project was the Airbus A350-1000, which would receive an additional fuel tank and a slightly increased maximum takeoff weight to deliver the required performance. The firm 12-aircraft order was confirmed in May 2022. In February 2024, Qantas announced a delay of roughly six months, which Airbus attributed to the need to redesign the extra fuel tank, moving delivery to mid-2026. Qantas's August 2025 full-year result expected deliveries from October 2026. Airbus's June 2026 program update set the first delivery for April 2027.

The aircraft has since demonstrated the capability the program requires. The first A350-1000ULR made its maiden flight on June 2, 2026, flying for 3 hours and 43 minutes over France. In July 2026, Airbus conducted two nonstop test flights between Toulouse and Melbourne using that aircraft, which were reported as setting a distance record for a commercial airliner. Qantas unveiled the aircraft at Toulouse on June 17, 2026, with the second airframe moving through an eight-week testing and certification program. Those test flights matter beyond the publicity, because they validated the modified fuel system and the extended-range systems that distinguish the ULR from a standard A350-1000 across a real mission profile rather than in a laboratory. The certification campaign covering those changes is what stands between the current flight testing and a delivered aircraft, and it is the piece of the program Qantas does not control.

The ultra-long 22-hour journey from Toulouse will be the longest flight of the test campaign to date.

Qantas will launch daily nonstop Sydney to London service in October 2027, the first Project Sunrise route, operating alongside the existing Perth to London and Sydney via Singapore to London services. Sydney to New York follows from mid-2028, which Qantas Group CEO Vanessa Hudson described as completing a vision the airline set out many years ago. The first aircraft is expected in April 2027, giving roughly six months between delivery and the opening revenue flight.

The route network it supports is also still expanding. Qantas confirmed Sydney to New York in September 2026, describing it as the first ever nonstop commercial service between Australia and New York, and Hudson called adding the city a defining moment for Australia and the United States. The airline has indicated further Project Sunrise destinations are possible beyond London and New York, which would push crew requirements even higher. Each additional ultra-long-haul route requires its own rostering coverage rather than drawing on spare capacity from existing ones, because a crew operating a 22-hour sector is unavailable for an extended period afterward.

The 360 and 1,200 figures are not a launch requirement. Qantas has said both groups will be trained by the time the twelfth A350-1000ULR arrives, a date the airline has not published and that depends on a delivery schedule that has already shifted several times. The workforce builds alongside the fleet rather than ahead of it, with each additional aircraft requiring another tranche of qualified crew. For the first route, Qantas needs enough crew to operate one daily rotation to London. For the full program across London, New York and whatever follows, it needs all 1,560.

#6275. KLM Plans 1,000 More Job Cuts

KLM expects to eliminate approximately 1,000 positions through productivity improvements as part of a restructuring announced Thursday.

The Dutch carrier said it would seek to limit the impact through natural attrition, voluntary arrangements and transfers. Other changes include moving about 800 ground services positions to outside providers and transferring 2,000 positions to Air France-KLM, including 1,500 at customer contact center Cygnific.

“But KLM’s future is not guaranteed,” CEO Marjan Rintel said in a statement, citing global instability, high fuel prices, and pressure on the industry.

KLM is targeting a structural productivity increase of at least 8% by 2028, alongside restrained wage growth. It said an additional €1 billion in annual earnings improvement is needed to fund investments.

The changes also affect its European fleet. KLM will replace planned Airbus A320s with Embraer E195-E2s, giving regional subsidiary Cityhopper a larger role. The A321neo will remain, while Boeing 737s and Embraer E190s will be phased out.

The announcement came as KLM reported a third-quarter operating profit of €458 million, up from €352 million a year earlier. For the first nine months of 2026, operating profit reached €526 million on revenue of €10.9 billion.

Despite the improvement, KLM said profitability remains insufficient to support its investment needs. Higher fuel costs and Middle East flight cancellations weighed on its passenger business, while Transavia faced competition and operational challenges.

“We need to increase it to more than 8% to secure a financially healthy future for KLM,” Chief Financial Officer Bas Brouns said of the airline’s profit margin.

As High As 300,000 points. Find Out Your Offer.

As High As 175,000 points. Find Out Your Offer.

They say the best deals never last forever, and in the world of points and miles, that's unquestionably true.

And after a pretty great run, one of the best deals in travel is about to get much harder to earn.

Thanks to major changes coming to Southwest Rapid Rewards in 2027, the days of using big credit card welcome bonuses to quickly earn a Southwest Companion Pass are almost over.

That's a big deal because the Companion Pass lets you bring a designated companion along on Southwest flights for just the cost of taxes and fees, starting at $5.60 each way. And you can use it again and again and again while your pass is valid.

But there's some good news if you've been hoping to earn one the quick and easy way.

You still have one last chance to use Southwest credit card welcome bonuses to help unlock a Companion Pass that's valid through the end of 2027. And the timing is especially good right now because Southwest just increased the welcome offers on its credit cards.

For example, the (see rates and fees) is currently offering 90,000 bonus points after you spend $3,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening.

That's two-thirds of the 135,000 qualifying points needed to earn a Companion Pass under the current rules, just from one welcome bonus.

There's just one catch: You need to apply and be approved for an eligible Southwest credit card by Dec. 2, 2026, to take advantage of this opportunity.

Here's how to make this strategy work one last time before the rules change.

Related: Southwest Rapid Rewards: How to earn and redeem points, elite status and more

To earn a Southwest Companion Pass under the current rules, you need to earn 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points in a calendar year. Normally, all those points would need to post to your Southwest account by Dec. 31, but Southwest is making a special exception as it transitions to its new rules for 2027.

As long as you're approved for an eligible Southwest credit card by Dec. 2, 2026, its welcome-bonus points can still count toward qualification under the 2026 Companion Pass rules, even if they post in early 2027.

That means you have a little more time to meet the spending requirement and earn those bonus points. However, you still need to earn enough qualifying points from other eligible activities in 2026.

And importantly, if you aren't approved for a Southwest credit card by Dec. 2, 2026, the welcome bonus points won't count toward a Companion Pass under this special exception.

Here's an example of how this could work.

Let's say you've already earned 45,000 Companion Pass qualifying points in 2026 from flying Southwest or using eligible partners, such as hotels, rental cars and the Rapid Rewards shopping portal.

That leaves you needing another 90,000 qualifying points to unlock the pass — that's where the newly increased Southwest credit card offers come in.

If you apply for and are approved for the Southwest Rapid Rewards Priority Credit Card by Dec. 2, and then earn its 90,000-point welcome bonus after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first three months, you could have enough points to earn a Southwest Companion Pass valid through Dec. 31, 2027. The everyday spending you put on the card also earns points that can help you get closer to qualifying for the pass.

And once you earn the pass, you're able to bring your designated companion along on Southwest flights as often as you want in 2027, paying just the taxes and fees.

Of course, not everyone already has around 45,000 qualifying points earned in 2026. But there's potentially another way to earn enough points before this opportunity disappears.

The timing couldn't be much better if you're hoping to earn a Southwest Companion Pass before the rules change, as Southwest just increased the welcome offers on all five of its credit cards.

Here are the current offers to consider if you want to take advantage of this opportunity before the Dec. 2 deadline.

These are limited-time offers, and we don't yet know when they will end. And remember that you need to be approved by Dec. 2, 2026, to take advantage of the special rules allowing these welcome bonuses to count toward a Companion Pass under the current qualification requirements.

The information for the Southwest Rapid Rewards Premier Credit Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Let's say you aren't on track to earn enough points to qualify for a Southwest Companion Pass one last time with just the points from one Southwest credit card bonus.

A natural question from the creative set of points enthusiasts who want to go all-in on Southwest might be ... can you get two Southwest credit card bonuses to count in one year?

The short answer is yes — in one specific situation.

Under Chase's current application restrictions, you're generally ineligible for another Southwest personal card if you already hold one, and previous welcome bonuses can also affect your eligibility.

On top of that, you must have at least 24 months between Southwest personal card welcome bonuses. So if you got one in early 2026, you can't get another now in late 2026, even if you no longer have the first card.

However, having a Southwest personal card doesn't necessarily prevent you from qualifying for a Southwest business card, though Chase's 5/24 rule can still affect your eligibility.

The rules for Southwest business cards state that you cannot currently have that particular card and you cannot have received a welcome bonus on that particular card in the past 24 months.

So, depending on your eligibility, that means you could potentially combine the welcome bonuses from a Southwest personal card and a Southwest business card to earn enough points for a Companion Pass.

For example, the currently offers 80,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first three months, while the offers 60,000 bonus points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first three months.

That's a combined 140,000 bonus points, enough to reach the current 135,000-point Companion Pass threshold without even counting the points earned from meeting the spending requirements.

Southwest is in the process of dramatically reshaping its airline, its loyalty program and virtually everything in between. There will be lounges, a premium credit card and a more traditionally structured elite status program where the top tier comes with a Companion Pass.

And the credit cards will certainly play a large role in that reshaped airline well into the future.

But in the midst of all that change, we are looking down the barrel of a quickly approaching 'one last time' deadline if you want to get a Southwest credit card and have the welcome bonuses help you earn a Companion Pass.

Whether you're combining a bonus with points you've already earned or considering a personal and business card strategy, the key deadline is Dec. 2, 2026. You'll need to apply and be approved by then to take advantage of the special transition rules.

If you qualify, you could earn a Companion Pass valid through Dec. 31, 2027, allowing you to bring a designated companion on eligible Southwest flights for just the cost of taxes and fees.

#6273. Teamsters Sue Horizon Air Over Pilot Rest Rules

The Teamsters have sued Horizon Air, alleging the Alaska Air Group subsidiary violated federal labor law by changing how it handles pilots who report fatigue.

The Teamsters Airline Division and Local 1224 filed the lawsuit Oct. 23 in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington. The union alleges Horizon requires pilots who report fatigue at their home base to travel to another city as passengers before taking the rest provided under their contract.

The union alleges the practice violates the Railway Labor Act and is asking the court to order Horizon to stop it and restore the negotiated rest protections.

“Management cannot pick and choose which parts of our contract it wants to follow,” said Sean Lenney, a Horizon pilot and member of Local 1224, in a news release.

The Teamsters also said Thursday that 99% of pilots who voted backed a no-confidence measure against Carlos Zendejas, Horizon’s senior vice president of operations. The union’s Horizon Air Pilots Executive Council called for his removal following the vote.

Horizon and its pilots have been negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement for more than three and a half years, according to the union. Pilots held informational pickets in Seattle and Boise, Idaho, on Oct. 15 over issues including pay, staffing, and training.

#6272. Singapore Airlines Unveils New First & Business Class Cabins For A350, 777-9

The wait is finally over — Singapore Airlines has today unveiled its all-new cabins, which were first teased two years ago. Most significantly, this includes a brand new business class, plus the expansion of first class to more planes. This really represents the carrier’s next generation product offering, since these cabins will be installed on future Boeing 777-9s, as well as retrofitted on dozens of Airbus A350s.

Let’s first talk briefly about which planes will be getting this product, and then we’ll cover the details of the cabins. Keep in mind these changes will also include an updated soft product, including a new dining concept as well as new amenities across cabins.

Singapore Airlines’ new cabin products will be coming to all of the carrier’s upcoming Boeing 777-9s, as well as to select Airbus A350-900s. This includes a new first class, business class, premium economy, and economy, along with updated inflight entertainment and the installation of Starlink Wi-Fi.

Singapore Airlines has 31 Boeing 777-9s on order, which are expected to eventually be the carrier’s flagship aircraft. These will come delivered with the new cabins. As a matter of fact, Singapore Airlines had initially planned to debut the new cabins on these 777-9s all the way back in 2020. However, delivery of those planes has now been pushed back to late 2027 at the earliest.

More immediately, Singapore Airlines also plans to invest 1.1 billion SGD (~835 million USD) to update the interiors of its entire long haul Airbus A350-900 fleet. This consists of a total of 41 jets, and includes the carrier’s seven A350-900ULRs, with the “ULR” standing for “ultra long range,” as these planes operate the world’s longest flights.

The only A350-900s that won’t be reconfigured are the ones that are specifically designed for regional flights, featuring the same cabin products you’ll find onboard Boeing 787-10s.

How will the layouts of A350s change, once reconfigured? Singapore Airlines’ standard long haul A350-900s:

Singapore Airlines’ ultra long range A350-900s:

With the above out of the way, let’s take a look at Singapore Airlines’ new first class and business class seats. Let me say upfront that:

Below is a chart with the basics of Singapore Airlines’ new first class product.

Singapore Airlines’ new first class seat is designed by PriestmanGoode, and manufactured by Collins Aerospace, and it’ll be available exclusively on Boeing 777-9s and Airbus A350-900ULRS (so not on standard A350-900s, and it won’t be retrofitted on existing aircraft).

Entertainment will be available on a 32″ 4K monitor. As you’d expect, tech will be cutting edge beyond that, with bluetooth audio, wireless, AC, and USB-C charging, etc. There will also be a touchscreen handset that provides easy access to KrisWorld, plus a panel with seat controls and flight information.

One of the nice things is that the center suites have a retractable divider, potentially creating a large, expansive space, so that guests in the center seats can dine and relax together. Singapore Airlines claims that when combined, the double bed becomes the biggest bed in commercial aviation, as it measures 80″ long and 60″ wide.

There won’t be overhead bins in first class, so bags can be stored in a cabin baggage compartment underneath the seat. There will also be a personal wardrobe, and a leather-lined vanity drawer.

What’s my take on Singapore Airlines’ new first class? Quite honestly, this is almost exactly what I was expecting from the airline:

Below is a chart with the basics of Singapore Airlines’ new business class product.

Singapore Airlines’ new business class seat is designed by BMW Designworks, and manufactured by RECARO, and it’ll be available exclusively on Boeing 777-9s and Airbus A350-900s (both long haul and ultra long haul).

Entertainment will be available on a 20-22″ 4K monitor. As you’d expect, tech will be cutting edge beyond that, with bluetooth audio, wireless, AC, and USB-C charging, etc. The airline also highlights how the seat has multiple storage options, which is appreciated.

Perhaps what’s most interesting is how in every other row, the center seats will be very close together, with the ability to form a double bed, which is a feature that customers always appreciate.

What’s my take on Singapore Airlines’ new business class? In some ways it’s what I expected, but there are some real surprises here:

Maybe it’ll look different in person, but am I the only one who is genuinely confused by the color choices? Those yellow accents just feel very… Spirit Airlines or Scoot, no?

When can we expect Singapore Airlines’ new premium products to debut? The expectation is that we’ll see a long haul Airbus A350-900 reconfigured first, and the first of those planes should now enter service in the second quarter of 2027. We don’t yet have any details beyond that.

The expectation is that the first retrofitted A350-900ULR (the ultra long range plane, operating the world’s longest flight) will debut at some point later in 2027, though that’s still up in the air. Meanwhile the 777-9s should start to join the fleet in late 2027 or early 2028 — only time will tell, given never-ending delays with Boeing.

Singapore Airlines should finish retrofitting its 41 A350s with the new cabins by either 2030 or 2031, though that timeline also remains subject to change. The delays with these new products reflects industry-wide supply chain constraints, as well as delays in the certification of the new seats (a common industry problem). The aircraft will be retrofitted by SIA Engineering Company in Singapore.

Which routes are likely to get the new cabins first? While we’ll see how this plays out, based on historical precedent, it’s likely that Sydney (SYD) and London (LHR) will be the first two destinations, since those are the first destinations where the airline has sent all of its new long haul products.

Singapore Airlines has just unveiled all-new cabins, which includes a new first class and business class. These cabins will be retrofitted on select Airbus A350-900s, and installed on all factory fresh Boeing 777-9s. These new products are long overdue, and I can’t wait to see them in service.

In first class, Singapore Airlines opted for a product that feels on brand, with warm colors, and a functional design that even allows for a double suite in the center seats. Meanwhile in business class, the airline chose a staggered product that looks solid, but I just can’t get over the cabin finishes… maybe it’s just me.

What do you make of Singapore Airlines’ new long haul cabins?

#6271. PSA Pilots Secure Contract Extension Through 2030

PSA Airlines’ pilot union leaders have approved an agreement that extends the regional carrier’s pilot contract by two years and locks in three rounds of pay increases.

The Air Line Pilots Association announced the agreement Wednesday. It extends the existing contract through April 1, 2030. The previous extension, ratified in 2022, had set an amendable date of April 1, 2028.

Current pay rates will remain in place until June 1, 2027, when the first increases take effect. Additional raises are scheduled for June 1 in each of the following two years. The deal also changes scheduling and work rules. ALPA’s announcement did not specify the size of the raises or detail the scheduling changes.

“When we asked our pilots what mattered most, the answer was clear: Protect our pay. This agreement does that,” said Capt. Chris Sabia, who chairs the union’s PSA Master Executive Council, in a news release.

ALPA represents approximately 2,260 pilots at PSA, which is a wholly-owned regional subsidiary of American Airlines.
